title: Trace sampling budget and severity-weighted latency heatmap notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposed approach for two related observability efforts that have come up during recent incidents: (1) a principled trace sampling budget model that preserves high-fidelity traces for impactful errors and emergent regressions while bounding storage/ingest cost, and (2) a new dashboard widget we call the 'severity-weighted latency heatmap' to help SREs and engineers quickly surface where tail latency and functional severity coincide across tenants, models, and routes.

Context / Why now:
- Recent P1 (INF-2389) showed we missed correlated high CPU / token retries because our sampling dropped traces from low-volume tenants during the window.
- Current dashboards show either latency percentiles or error rates, but cross-slicing them by severity (customer impact) is manual and slow.
- We want an approach that: (a) keeps costs bounded, (b) preserves traces where debugging ROI is high, and (c) integrates with oncall workflows.

High-level goals:
- Define a sampling budget that is enforced per cluster/pool and adaptive by risk signal (error spikes, model change rollouts, SLO burn).
- Surface a single dashboard widget that highlights cells where 95th/99th latency is high AND incident severity is elevated (automatically weights by recent SLA impact).
- Make sampling and dashboard behavior configurable per-customer-tier and per-route (hosted vs dedicated).

Trace sampling model (proposal):
1) Baseline deterministic sampling for control-plane flows: keep 1:100 for routine requests (to avoid overwhelming storage).
2) Severity amplification: if a request results in an error classified as customer-impacting (status codes + correlation to fallback behavior), amplify sampling to 1:1 for that request's trace context and sibling requests for the next N seconds (default N=120).
3) SLO-burn amplification: if SLO burn for a route or tenant exceeds threshold (e.g., 10% burn in 5m), automatically increase sampling multiplier for that route to capture more traces for root-cause analysis.
4) Canary/rollout sticky sampling: during model rollouts (A/B/canary), sample all canary traffic at 1:1 for the rollout window; downgrade to baseline after validation.
5) Reservoir budget per node-group: enforce a daily/event reservoir (e.g., 10k traces/day/node) to avoid blowups. Controller reduces sampling multipliers if reservoir usage exceeds 80%.
6) Low-volume tenant preservation: retain higher fraction for tenants with <X qps if they trigger errors, to avoid losing context for small customers.

Implementation notes / telemetry hooks needed:
- Add two new labels to traces: sampling_reason (enum: baseline, severity_amp, slo_amp, rollout, low_volume) and sampling_token (unique id for reservoir accounting).
- Metric: trace.ingest.count by sampling_reason and node_group (counter).
- Metric: trace.reservoir.usage_ratio per node_group (gauge).
- Event: sampling_budget.throttle.triggered with tags {node_group, route, tenant}.
- Expose short-lived API to temporarily pin sampling multipliers for an owner (used by SE/Oncall).

Edge cases and open questions:
- Correlated burst of errors across many tenants might exhaust reservoir quickly; should we prioritize by tenant revenue/SL tier? (proposal: yes — add tenant_priority bucket).
- Privacy: private deployments should default to local-only trace retention; sampling decisions must respect tenant policies.
- Do we store full spans for 1:1 samples or can we compact older traces? Need retention/compaction plan tied to sampling_reason.
- Implementation complexity: how to wire sampling controller into the runtime with minimal latency impact? Option: sampling decision deferred to async span-collector service with fast-path headers set by the runtime.

Severity-weighted latency heatmap (widget design):
What it is:
- A 2D heatmap grid where X axis = route/model (grouped), Y axis = tenant segment (all, high-touch, freemium), cell color intensity = weighted_score. Weighted_score = alpha * latency_tail + beta * severity_score + gamma * error_rate, normalized by traffic volume. Default alpha=0.6, beta=0.3, gamma=0.1 (tunable).

Inputs required:
- latency distribution metrics (p50/p95/p99) per route/model/tenant (existing).
- error counts by code and a derived severity_score (mapping: circuit_trip/fallback=0.9, generation_error=0.7, mild-qa=0.2).
- traffic volume to normalize (qps).
- recent SLO burn (5m) as multiplier for weighting.

Interactivity / drilldown:
- Hover a cell -> sparkline of p50/p95/p99 + error-rate trend; quick-link to traces sampled for that cell (filtered by sampling_reason != baseline).
- Click cell -> open pre-filtered Trace Explorer with suggested span anchors (see 'anchoring' below) and top correlated logs.
- Filter top-N by weighted_score, or sort rows by max cell value.

Span anchoring / trace design for dashboard drilldown:
- Define 3 canonical span anchors to ease root-cause navigation:
  1) request/ingress (client metadata, route, model_version)
  2) runtime/kv-cache (cache.hit, cache.latency_us, cache.key_type)
  3) generation/decoder (tokens_out, generation_latency_ms, quantization_variant)
- For each span anchor include small structured tags to link to metric dimensions: tenant_id, route_id, model_id, batch_size, sequence_length_bucket.
- Trace Explorer should default to grouping by the runtime/kv-cache spans when investigating prefix-related regressions.

Dashboard placement and layout guidance:
- Place the severity-weighted heatmap on the top-right of the infra overview page (near SLO burn and per-route latency cards).
- Widget size recommendation: 4x3 grid card for 12 models x 6 tenant segments (responsive).
- Provide a toggle to view by 'per-tenant' or 'per-cluster'.

Operational runbook snippets (for oncall):
- When a heatmap cell exceeds threshold:
  1) Click -> open Trace Explorer; if sampling_reason != baseline, pick top traces and check span anchors.
  2) Run quick checks: recent deploys (release-engineering PR list), model version pins, autoscaler events.
  3) If traces sparse: escalate to sampling-controller to temporarily boost sampling for the route (one-click action).

Ownership & rollout plan (30/60/90):
- 0-30d: prototype sampling_reason labels + local reservoir accounting in telemetry service. Create dashboard mock in Grafana using synthetic score. (owner: Marcus Li)
- 30-60d: integrate sampling-controller with runtime; implement severity amplification and SLO-burn hooks; add oncall UI control. (owner: Diego Alvarez)
- 60-90d: iterate on weighting coefficients from real incidents; document runbooks and add automated alert that recommends sampling boosts when needed. (owner: eng-observability lead)

Action items (next steps):
- [Marcus] PR for trace label schema and test vectors (github PR #412).
- [Riya] Draft Grafana dashboard panel JSON for the initial heatmap and share with SRE for feedback.
- [Diego] Spike: measure latency impact of injecting sampling headers in runtime (target <500us p99 overhead).
- [Leah] Add an entry to the observability playbook with the runbook snippets and escalate flow.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- We should avoid calling the widget a 'risk map' internally — people will over-index on it. 'Severity-weighted latency heatmap' is verbose but descriptive.
- Consider tying reservoir prioritization to customer-revenue buckets (needs privacy/legal review).
- Short-term hack: if we can't get reservoir controller in place fast, add a per-cluster kill-switch that lowers all non-severity sampling to 0.01 during cost spikes.

References & links:
- Jira: INF-2389 (incident notes)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412 (trace label schema)
- Confluence draft: obs/heatmap-design-proposal

Open questions for the next review meeting:
- Acceptable per-node reservoir size? (ops input required)
- Default alpha/beta/gamma values — should we A/B test the weighting?
- How do we ensure private deployments don't silently diverge in sampling behavior?
